count-compare-1000-skill-01.target: I can count forward and backward within 1,000, including across tens and hundreds.
count-compare-1000-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can count forward and backward within 1,000, including across tens and hundreds.
count-compare-1000-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Getting stuck when the count crosses a hundred (198, 199, 1,000) or a ten (409, 4,010). Try this: Count with base-ten blocks and trade; use a 1–1,000 number line and say the hundreds aloud.

count-compare-1000-skill-02.target: I can skip count by 5s, 10s, and 100s from any starting number and continue the pattern.
count-compare-1000-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can skip count by 5s, 10s, and 100s from any starting number and continue the pattern.
count-compare-1000-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Switching to counting by 1s or by 10s partway through, especially across a hundred. Try this: Name which digit changes for each jump (ones for 5s, tens for 10s, hundreds for 100s) and check it.

count-compare-1000-skill-03.target: I can compare two three-digit numbers using hundreds, tens, and ones and record it with >, =, or <.
count-compare-1000-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can compare two three-digit numbers using hundreds, tens, and ones and record it with >, =, or <.
count-compare-1000-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Comparing digit by digit from the ones place, or thinking a number with bigger digits anywhere is greater (189 > 201). Try this: Start with the hundreds; only look at the tens when the hundreds are equal. Read the symbol from left to right.

count-compare-1000-skill-04.target: I can mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to a number from 100 to 900.
count-compare-1000-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to a number from 100 to 900.
count-compare-1000-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Changing the wrong digit (adding 10 to the ones), or not regrouping when the tens digit is 9 (395 + 10 = 3,105). Try this: Use base-ten blocks: adding 10 means one more rod. Ask “Which place changed, and by how much?”
